90:1: God Almighty says: I swear, O Muhammad, by this city, which is Mecca. And the scholars of interpretation said the same. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, I swear by this city, meaning: Mecca. Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Waki’ told us, he said: On the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, I swear by this city, he said: Mecca. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: I swear by this city. He said: The Sacred City. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: I swear by this city. He said: Mecca. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: I swear by this city. He said: The city is Mecca. Suwar bin Abdullah told us, Qabil: Yahya bin Saad told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Ata’, regarding his statement, I swear by this city, meaning Mecca. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Yazid said, regarding God’s statement, I swear by this city, he said: Mecca.
90:2: And His statement: And you are a resident of this city means: in Mecca. God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And you, O Muhammad, are a resident of this city, meaning Mecca. He says: You are permitted to do in it whoever you want to kill, and take captive whoever you want to take captive. All of that is yours. It is said from it: He is permitted, and he is permitted, and he is forbidden. He is forbidden, and he is a place, and he is forbidden. And He made us permissible, and He made us forbidden. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And you are a resident of this city, meaning by that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. God made it permissible for him on the day he entered Mecca to kill whomever he wanted and spare whomever he wanted. So on that day he killed Ibn Khatal in a fit of rage while holding on to the curtains of the Kaaba. So it was not permissible for anyone after the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to kill in it someone forbidden by God. So God made permissible for him what he did to the people of Mecca. Have you not heard that God said about the sanctity of the sanctuary, And Hajj to the House is a duty owed to God by those who can afford the expenses for one’s expenses (Al Imran 3:97) meaning by the people the people of the Qiblah. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: And you are abiding in this country. He said: Whatever you do, you are absolved from the matter of fighting. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: And you are permitted to do this city. He said: Whatever he did in it for an hour was permitted to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: And you are a resident of this country. He said: It is permissible for him to do whatever he wants in it. Abu Kurayb told us, he said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, And you are permitted to do this in this country. He said: It was made permissible for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Do whatever you wish in it. Musa bin Abdul Rahman told me: Husayn Al-Ja’fi told us, on the authority of Za’idah, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, And you are absolved from this city, he said: You are absolved from what you did in it. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid: And you are permitted to do this in this country. He said: God has made permissible for you, O Muhammad, whatever you do in this country, meaning Mecca. Hamad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And you are a resident of this country, he said: You will not be held accountable for what you do in it, and you will not be held accountable for what people do in it. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And you are a resident of this country, meaning you are free from embarrassment and sin. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And you are a resident of this country. He said: And you are a resident of it, you are not sinful. Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb delayed us, he said: Ibn Yazid said, regarding His statement, And you are permitted to enter this city, he said: No one was permitted to enter it except the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Everyone who was in it was forbidden, it was not permissible for them to fight in it, nor to violate its sanctity, so God made it permissible for His Messenger, so he fought the polytheists in it. Suwar bin Abdullah told us: Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Ata’, And you are permitted to enter this country. He said: God made Mecca sacred. It was not permitted to any prophet except your prophet for an hour of the day. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding his statement, And you are residing in this city, meaning Muhammad, saying: You are residing in the sanctuary, so kill if you wish, or leave it.
90:3: And His saying: And by a father and what he begot, God Almighty says: So He swears by a father and by his son whom he begot. Then the people of interpretation differed about the meaning of that from the father and what he gave birth to. Some of them said: What is meant by the father is every father, and what he gave birth to is every barren woman who did not give birth. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Atiyah told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And a father and what he begot. He said: The father is the one who gives birth, and what he begot is the barren woman who has no children. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And the father and what he gave birth to. He said: The barren woman and the one who gives birth. Abu Kurayb told us, he said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Al-Nadr bin Arabi, on the authority of Ikrimah: And the father and what was born, he said: the barren woman and the one who gives birth. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And a father and what he begot. He said: It is the father and his son. Others said: He meant by that: Adam and his son. Who said that? Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And a father and what he begot. He said: The father is Adam, and what he begot is his son. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us. And Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, and a father and what he fathered, he said: his son. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And a father and what he begot. He said: Adam and what he begot. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada: And a father and what he begot. He said: Adam and what he begot. Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Salih, regarding his statement, And a father and what he begot, he said: Adam and what he begot. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say, regarding His statement, and a father and what he begot, he said: The father is Adam, and what he begot is his son. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan, regarding his statement, and a father and what he begot, he said: Adam and what he begot. Yunus bin Abdul-A’la told me: Muhammad bin Ubaid told us on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Salih, regarding his statement, And a father and what he begot, he said: Father and what he begot. Others said: What he meant by that was: Abraham and what he had born. Who said that? Muhammad bin Musa Al-Harshi told me, he said: Jaafar bin Sulayman told us, he said: I heard Abu Imran Al-Joni reading and a father and what he begot. He said: Abraham and what he begot. The correct statement about this is what was said by those who said: God swore by every parent and his parent, because God is general in every parent and what is born. It is not permissible to make this specific except with a proof that must be accepted from a report or reason. There is no report that specifies this, nor is there proof that must be accepted specifically in this regard. So it is general in its generality as it is general in its generality.
90:4: And His saying: Indeed, We created man into hardship. This is the answer to the oath. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: The oath Indeed, We created man into hardship occurred here. The commentators differed in their interpretation of this. Some of them said: It means: We created the son of Adam in hardship, distress, and fatigue. Who said that? Ali told us, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Indeed, We created man into hardship, meaning: into fatigue. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us, he said: Sa`id told us, on the authority of Mansur Ibn Zadhan, on the authority of Al-Hasan, that he said regarding this verse, Indeed, We created man into hardship, meaning: in hardship. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Indeed, We created man into hardship. When he was created in difficulty, the son of Adam encounters nothing but the struggles of the affairs of this world and the hereafter. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, in the burden of life, he said: The burden of the affairs of this world and the hereafter. Some of them said: He created a creation whose creation we did not create at all. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Ali bin Rifa’ah, who said: I heard Al-Hasan say: God did not create a creation that endures what the son of Adam endures. He said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Ali bin Rafa’ah, who said: I heard Saeed bin Abi Al-Hasan say: Indeed, We created man in hardship. He said: He suffers the calamities of this world and the hardships of the Hereafter. He said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Al-Nadr, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: Indeed, We created man into hardship. He said: In hardship. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Indeed, We created man into hardship. He said: In hardship. He said: Mahran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: In the hardship of his livelihood, his burden, his life, and the growth of his teeth. He said: Mahran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, Mujahid said, Man is in a state of suffering. He said: The severity of his teeth coming out. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Man is in hardship, he said, hardship. Others said: This means that he was created erect and of moderate height. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Indeed, We created man into hardship, he said: in an erect position, and it is said: in hardship. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Harami bin Ammarah told us: Shu’bah told us: Ammarah told me, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding His statement, Indeed, We created man into toil, he said: In an upright position, meaning stature. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, Indeed, We created man into toil. He said: Upright. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, and Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Waki’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, the same. Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaddad, regarding his statement, Indeed, We created man into toil, he said: Of moderate stature. Abu Saleh said: Of moderate stature. Yahya bin Dawud Al-Wasiti told us: Yahya bin Saeed Al-Qattan told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Saleh: We created man in toil. He said: Standing. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: I heard Abu Muadh saying: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say, regarding His statement, in a liver, that He was created erect on two legs. No animal was created with His creation. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Mujahid: Indeed, We created man into toil. He said: In hardship. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that he was created in heaven. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said in his Qulūlah, Indeed, We created man in toil. He said: In the sky, that is called the toil. The most correct of the sayings is the one that says: The meaning of this is that he was created to struggle with money and deal with it, so his saying in struggle means: in hardship. We said that this is more correct, because this is what is known in the speech of the Arabs as meanings of the liver, and from it is the saying of Labid bin Rabi’ah: Ain Hala, I cried for Arbid when we stood up and the opponents stood up in the liver
90:5: And His saying: Does he think that no one will have power over him? It was mentioned that this was revealed regarding a specific man from Banu Jumah, who was called Abu al-Ashdayn, and he was strong. So the Most High said: Does this strong man, with his strength and power, think that no one will conquer him and overcome him? But God is the One who will conquer him and subdue him.
90:6: And his saying: He says I wasted a lot of money This very cold person says: I wasted a lot of money, in the custom of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and I spent it on it, and he is lying in what he says. It is an action from the verb talbadd, which means to pile up some of it on top of others, and it is said from it: labad on the ground, yalbad: if he stuck to it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Money that is abundant means by money that is abundant. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Mala Labada he said: A lot. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Muslim told me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, I have destroyed wealth in abundance, he said: A great deal of wealth. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, I have wasted a great deal of wealth means a great deal. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, the same. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, in his statement, much is not to be missed. He said, Much is missed. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of the regions recited it as mala labda with a light ba, and Abu Jaafar recited it with a heavy ba. The correct pronunciation is to pronounce it lightly, as the evidence is unanimously agreed upon.
90:7: And His statement: Does he think that no one saw him? God Almighty says: Does this person who says I have wasted wealth in abundance think that no one saw him while he was spending what he claims he spent? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Does he think that no one sees him? O son of Adam, you are responsible for this money: from where you acquired it and where you spent it. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, the same.
90:8: God Almighty says: Did We not give this speaker, I have wasted wealth in abundance, two eyes with which to see God’s proofs against him, a tongue with which to express himself as he intended, and two lips, as a blessing from Us to him? Bishr urged us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: Have We not made for him two eyes?
90:9: And His saying: And a tongue and lips are blessings from God that are evident, and He acknowledges them to you so that you may thank Him.
90:10: And His statement: And We showed him the two ways, God Almighty says: And We showed him the two ways, and Najd is a way in a high place. The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of that. Some of them said: What is meant by that is: We find good and we find evil, as He said: Indeed, We showed him the way, be he grateful or ungrateful (al-Insan 76:3) Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Abdullah: And We guided him to the two ways. He said: Good and evil. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Abdullah, similarly. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Mundhir, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ar-Rabi` ibn Khathim, who said: They are not breasts. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, and Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Hakam told us, he said: Imran told us all, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Abdullah, And We guided him to the two ways, he said: Najd is good and Najd is evil. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Hisham bin Abdul-Malik told us: Shu’bah told us: Asim told me: I heard Abu Wa’il say: Abdullah used to say about And We guided him to the two ways: Najd is good and Najd is evil. Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And We guided him to the two ways, meaning: guidance and misguidance. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And We guided him to the two ways, meaning: the path of good and evil. Hanad bin Al-Sarri told us: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, And We guided him to the two ways, he said: good and evil. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Rabi’ ibn Khathim, on the authority of Abu Burdah, who said: Al-Rabi’ ibn Khathim passed by us, so we asked him about this verse: And We guided him to the two ways. He said: They are not breasts. Abu Kuraib told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Good and evil. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And We showed him the two ways, he said: The path of good and evil. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And We guided him to the two ways, the way of good and the way of evil. Imran bin Musa told us, he said: Abdul-Warith told us, he said: Yunus told us on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “They are two Najds, one is good and the other is evil. But the evil Najd is not more beloved to you than the good Najd.” Mujahid bin Musa told us, he said: Yazid bin Harun told us, he said: Atiyah Abu Wahb told us, he said: I heard Al-Hasan say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Behold, there are only two Najds: the Najd of good and the Najd of evil. So what makes the Najd of evil more beloved to you than the Najd of good?” Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Hisham bin Abdul-Malik told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, he said: I heard Al-Hasan say, And We showed him the two ways. He said: He told us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say, “O people, they are only the two ways: the way of good and the way of evil. So the way of evil has not been made more beloved to you than the way of good.” Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, And We guided him to the two Najds. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: “O people, they are only the two Najds: the Najd of good and the Najd of evil. So the Najd of evil has not been made more beloved to you than the Najd of good.” Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding His statement, And We showed him the two ways, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They are only two ways, so He has not made the evil way more beloved to you than the good way. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb delayed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, in his statement, And We guided him to the two ways, he is a highwayman of good and evil, and he recited the statement of God, Indeed, We guided him to the way (al-Insan 76:3). Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: And We guided him to the two breasts: the two paths of milk with which he is nourished, and on which his flesh and body grow. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Waki` told us, he said: Isa bin Uqal told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And We guided him to the two ways. He said: They are the two breasts. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Al-Mubarak bin Mujahid, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, who said: The breasts. The more correct of the two opinions on this matter in our view is the opinion of those who said: He meant by that the path of good and evil, because we do not know of any opinion on this matter other than the two opinions that we have mentioned. And the breasts, even if the path is milk, then when God Almighty enumerated His blessings upon the servant in His saying, “Indeed, We created man from a sperm-drop mixture that We may try him; and We made him hearing and seeing. Indeed, We guided him to the way” (al-Insan 76:2-3), He only enumerated His guidance of him to the path of good among His blessings. So too is His saying, And We guided him to the two ways.
90:11: And His statement: So he did not take the steep path, God Almighty says: So he did not climb the steep path, cross it, or go over it. And He mentioned that the steep path is a mountain in Hell. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Yahya bin Katheer told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, So do not attempt the steep path, he said: A steep path in Hell. Omar bin Ismail bin Mujalid told me: Abdullah bin Idris told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Atiyah, on the authority of Ibn Omar, regarding his statement, So he did not attempt the steep path, meaning a mountain in Hell. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, So do not attempt the steep path, he said: Hell. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, So do not attempt the difficult path, is that it is a difficult path, so attempt it in obedience to God. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: So do not take the steep path. He said: The Fire has a steep path before the bridge. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Wahb ibn Jarir told us, he said: My father told us, he said: I heard Yahya ibn Ayoub narrating on the authority of Yazi ibn Abi Habib, on the authority of Shu’ayb ibn Zur’ah, on the authority of Hanash, on the authority of Ka’b, that he said: So do not attempt the steep path. He said: It is seventy degrees in Hell. He singled out his statement, So he did not storm the pass, by mentioning the word la only once. The Arabs rarely single it out in a statement in such a place, until they repeat it with another statement, as He said, Neither did he believe nor did he pray (Al-Qiyamah 29:31), and nor will there be any fear concerning them, nor will they grieve (Al-Baqarah 2:112). He did that in this place, as the meaning of the end of the statement is sufficient, so as not to repeat it again. That is when he explains storming the pass, he says, The freeing of a slave, or the feeding on a day of famine, an orphan near of kin, or a needy person covered with dust, then he was among those who believed. So he explained that with three things, so it was as if he was at the beginning of the statement, saying, So he did not do this or that. Ibn Zayd interpreted that to mean, Why not? And whoever interprets it in this way has no need to claim that there is something omitted in the statement. The report was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Zayd: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, and he recited the words of God, So he did not attempt the steep path. He said: Why did he not take the path from which there is salvation and goodness? Then he said, And what will make you know what the steep path is?
90:12: And His saying: And what will make you know what the obstacle is? God Almighty says: And what will make you know, O Muhammad, what the obstacle is? Then He, the Most High, explained to him what the obstacle was, what the escape from it was, and what the reason for storming it was. He said: Storming it and cutting it frees a neck from slavery and the captivity of servitude. Yaqoub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, And what will make you know what the Aqaba is? He said: It was mentioned to us that no Muslim frees a Muslim slave, except that it is his ransom from the Fire. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Sa’i told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And what will make you know what the difficult path is? * The freeing of a slave. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about slaves, which one has the greatest reward? The one with the greatest price. Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatadah, he said: Salim bin Abi Al-Ja’d narrated to us, on the authority of Adan bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Abu Nujayh, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, say: “Any Muslim who frees a Muslim man, God will make the ransom for every bone of his atonement a bone of the one he frees from the Fire. And any Muslim woman who frees a Muslim woman, God will make the ransom for every bone of hers a bone of the one she frees from the Fire.” He said: Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Qays Al-Jadhami, on the authority of Uqbah bin Amir Al-Juhani, that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Whoever frees a believing slave, she will be his ransom from the Fire. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And what will make you know what the Aqaba is? Then he told about storming it and said: Free a slave or feed. The reciters differed in reading this. Some of the reciters of Mecca and the majority of the reciters of Basra read it, on the authority of Ibn Abi Ishaq. Among the Kufians: Al-Kisa’i read it as freeing a slave or feeding. Abu Amr ibn Al-Ala’ used to provide evidence, but what I have heard about him is his statement, Then he was among those who believed (al-Balad 90:17). It is as if its meaning was with him: He did not free a slave, nor did he feed, then he was among those who believed. The majority of the reciters of Medina, Kufa and Ash-Sham read it as freeing a slave with the addition, and or feeding with the form of a verbal noun. The reward for saying this is that they are two well-known readings, each of which has been recited by scholars of recitation and an understood interpretation. Whichever one the reciter recites, he is correct. If it is recited as a verb, its interpretation is: So he did not storm the steep path, “No, he freed a slave,” or No, he fed, “Then he was among those who believed.” And what will make you know what the steep path is? expresses amazement and glorification. This reading is better expressed in Arabic, because feeding is a noun, and His saying, Then he was among those who believed is a verb, and the Arabs prefer to return nouns to nouns like them, and verbs to verbs. If the revelation had come, Then if he was among those who believed, it would have been better and more similar to feeding and freeing from then it was. That is why I said, Freeing a slave or feeding has more meaning in Arabic than the other, even though the other has a well-known meaning, and its meaning is to imply that then is received, as Tarafa ibn al-Abd said: Oh you who deter! I am preparing for battle and witnessing pleasures. Will you make me immortal? Meaning: O you who forbid me to attend the battle. And in His saying that I bear witness there is clear evidence that it is conjoined with another like it, which came before it, and that is the reason for its permissibility. And if the speech is directed in this way then his saying freeing a slave * or feeding is an explanation of his saying And what will make you know what the difficult path is? As if it was said: And what will make you know what the difficult path is? It is freeing a slave.
90:13: God Almighty said: Freeing a slave.
90:14: His statement: Or feeding on a day of famine, as the Most High said: And what will make you know what it is? (al-Qari’ah 101:10) Then he said: A blazing fire. (al-Qari’ah 101:11), explaining his statement: And his mother is the abyss. (al-Qari’ah 101:9) Then he said: And what will make you know what the abyss is? It is a blazing fire. His saying or feed on a day of famine means: or feed on a day of famine, and the hungry one is the one who is hungry. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas or feed on a day of famine: a day of famine. Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us: Khalid bin Hayyan Al-Raqi Abu Yazid told me, on the authority of Jaafar bin Barqan, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding the words of God or feed on a day of famine, he said: a day of famine. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, On a day of famine, he said: Hunger. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement or feed on a day of famine means: a day on which food is desired. Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Uthman Al-Thaqafi, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, On a day of famine. He said: Famine. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Uthman ibn al-Mughira, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the same. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, On a day of famine, that he said: Famine.
90:15: And his saying: An orphan of near relation means: Or he fed on a day of famine a young child who has no father from among his relatives, and he is the orphan of near relation, and by of near relation he meant: the relative. As Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Yazi said regarding his statement, an orphan of near kinship, he said: of kinship.
90:16: And his saying: Or a poor person covered with dust. The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of his saying covered with dust. Some of them said: By that he meant: someone who clings to the dust. Who said that? Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, who said: Al-Mughirah told me, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Or a poor person covered with dust. He said: The one who has no shelter except dust. Mutraf bin Muhammad Al-Dhabi told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Mughirah, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the same. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Or a poor person covered with dust, he said: The one who is covered only by dust. Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida told me: Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-Mughirah, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He who is covered with dust means: He who has no protector but dust. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told me, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: A poor man covered in dust. He said: The one who has no shelter except dust. He said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Or a poor person covered in dust, he said, The poor person means the one lying in the dust. Abu Hasin told me, he said: Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Yunus told us, he said: Abthar told us, on the authority of Hasin, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Or a poor person covered with dust, he said: The one who has nothing to protect him from the dust. Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Hasin and Al-Mughira both told us, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said regarding His statement, Or a poor person covered with dust, he said: He is one who is stuck to the dust due to extreme poverty. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Abi Qais, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Or a poor person covered with dust. He said: Dust thrown on the road by the sweeper. Abu Kuraib told us: Talq bin Ghannam told us, on the authority of Zaidah, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Or a poor person covered with dust. He said: He is the poor person lying in the dust on the road. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Hussain, on the authority of Mujahid: Or a poor person covered with dust. He said: The one who is thrown to the ground, who is not protected by anything but the dust. Abu Kurayb told us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Or a poor person covered with dust. He said: He is one who is stuck to the ground, with nothing of the dust protecting him. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hisin and Uthman ibn al-Mughira, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Or a poor person covered with dust. He said: The one who has nothing to protect him from the dust. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, that which is covered in dust, he said: fallen in the dust. Abu Kurayb told us, he said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Ja’far bin Burqan, he said: Ikrimah heard, Or a poor person covered with dust, he said: One who clings to the ground out of need. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: Or a poor person covered with dust, he said: Dust sticking to the ground. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Uthman ibn al-Mughira, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The one who is thrown on the road and has no home but the dust. Others said: Rather, he is the one in need, whether he is stuck to the dirt or not. They said that it is from their saying: A man is in the dirt if he is poor. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Or a poor person covered with dust, he said: One in dire need. Hanad bin Al-Sarri told us: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, Or a poor person covered with dust, he said: He is the one who has no money. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Or a poor person covered with dust, he said: in need, dust means the needy. Others said: Rather, he is the one with many children who have become stuck to the ground due to hardship and severe need. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Or a poor man covered with dust, meaning: a poor man with children and dependents, with no kinship between you and him. Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Abi al-Mughira, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, regarding his statement: Or a poor person covered with dust, he said: One with a family. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Or a poor person covered with dust. We used to say that the one covered with dust is the one with dependents who has nothing. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Or a poor person covered with dust, “one with children clinging to the ground,” from poverty and hardship. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said: He meant by it: or a poor person who has been covered in dust from the poor and the needy, because that is the apparent meaning of it. And his saying covered with dust is maf’ala from the word tarab dirt of a man: if he is covered in dust.
90:17: God Almighty says: Then this one who said, I have destroyed wealth in abundance was among those who believed in God and His Messenger, so he believed with them as they believed. And they enjoined upon one another patience meaning: And among those who enjoined upon one another patience over what befell them for the sake of God. And they enjoined upon one another compassion meaning: And they enjoined upon one another compassion. Muhammad bin Sinan Al-Qazzaz told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Shabib, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And enjoin one another to compassion, he said: compassion for people.
90:18: And his saying, Those are the companions of the right hand, means: Those who did these actions that I mentioned, such as freeing slaves, feeding orphans, and other things, are the companions of the right hand, who will be taken on the Day of Resurrection to the right hand and into Paradise.
90:19: And His statement: And those who disbelieve in Our signs means: And those who disbelieve in Our proofs, Our signs, and Our arguments from the Books, the Messengers, and other than that. They are the companions of the left means: They are the companions of the left on the Day of Resurrection who will be taken to the left. We have already explained the meaning of the left, and why the left is called the left, previously, so there is no need to repeat it here.
90:20: And His statement, A closed fire will be upon them, God Almighty says: The fire of Hell will be closed upon them on the Day of Resurrection. It is said from this: I closed it and I closed it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, upon them is a closed fire, he said: closed. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Upon them is a closed fire. He said: Closed. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Upon them is a closed fire, meaning: sealed, God closed it over them, so there is no light in it, no relief, and no exit from it until the end of eternity. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say about closed: closed upon them.
